correctness.rationale: For W=P^k, greedy embedding advances copies exactly at weak descents, so v occurs iff D(v)≤k-1. Minimal absence forces D(v)=k, endpoint weak descents, and every interior Δ_i=d(v_{i-1},v_i)+d(v_i,v_{i+1})-d(v_{i-1},v_{i+1})=1. Ascents are isolated and induce strict two-step increases in BOTH parity tracks; with a ascents, remaining k-a-1 nonincreasing two-step edges imply k≥a+1+2floor((a-1)/(q-1)). Doubled staircase blocks T_h=00 11 ... (h-1)(h-1), repeated and supplemented with leading zeros, attain each allowed ascent count. Inverting gives exactly lengths k+1 to k+1+(q-1)floor((k-1)/(q+1))+min((k-1) mod(q+1),q-1), q≥4. Independently brute-forced all candidate MAS for q=4,k=1,2,3: length supports {2},{3,4},{4,5,6}, respectively, agreeing. Inspected separate finite-state/literal verifier, not using its output as universal proof.
residual_risks: General proof depends on parity-track and staircase construction; finite host checks alone cannot establish unbounded k or q.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General O(n log sigma) longest-MAS algorithm can compute each finite input but does not yield the symbolic q,k sharp length interval. Published ternary enumerator is a q=3 special alphabet outside q≥4. Neither dominates all arbitrary q≥4.

value.rationale: Permutation powers are natural canonical subsequence hosts; the exact contiguous spectrum of minimal absent lengths and sharp longest-length slope 2q/(q+1) solve a meaningful all-parameter combinatorial invariant. The parity-track obstruction and explicit extremal staircase witnesses provide structural interpretation beyond generic instance-by-instance algorithms.

limitations: q≥4, exact powers of one permutation over its full alphabet, all k≥1; determines possible lengths, not multiplicities. Finite corroboration does not establish infinite universal quantifiers.
